briefs.source_chain: Power shortfall (57GW gross/32GW net/34%) is real, confirmed by Nvidia itself, therefore MS stays convicted NVDA/AVGO hit their combined ~$800bn 12-month outlook (visibility into placement, geographic diversification, tokens-per-watt), therefore if a slowdown hits it's memory/optics/small-dollar components and ASICs (losing share to GPUs) that absorb it, not NVDA/AVGO, therefore power access concentrates to large credit-worthy hyperscalers/neoclouds (60-95% of capacity adds), squeezing smaller/international/ASIC players (Google specifically challenged by its own incremental build), therefore upside hinges on BTM (11-49GW, 19GW base) and international expansion, but neither closes the US gap (US compute share cut to 55% from 60%), capped further by labor and political constraints.

briefs.source_chain: AI buildout collides with a grid that can't deliver fast enough, inference shifts to smaller/closer-to-user nodes, and political resistance makes mega-campuses harder to scale, therefore MS expects a structural shift to BTM power; it forecasts 160GW incremental US DC demand 2026-29 (22GW under construction, 36GW available grid, 23GW BTM already procured, leaving a 77GW shortfall filled by SOFCs/gas engines/turbines); MS introduces SCACP (LCOE + idle-GPU opportunity cost) ranking Bloom SOFC #1, BorgWarner turbine #2, FTAI aeroderivative #3; the grid still serves 1GW+ training campuses while BTM targets smaller inference nodes and C&I demand (40GW incremental through 2029, $240bn/120GW BTM TAM); storage/VPPs (Sunrun+Tesla dispatched 580MW from 140k+ batteries during a Sept heat wave) complement generation; political pushback reinforces rather than reverses the BTM shift.
briefs.brief_chain: Grid can't deliver fast enough + inference shifts to smaller/closer nodes + political resistance to mega-campuses -> structural shift to BTM power/storage -> 160GW incremental demand 2026-29 (22GW under construction, 36GW available grid, 23GW BTM procured, 77GW shortfall filled by SOFC/gas engines/turbines) -> SCACP ranks Bloom SOFC #1, BorgWarner #2, FTAI #3 -> grid still serves 1GW+ campuses, BTM targets smaller inference + C&I (40GW/2029, $240bn/120GW TAM) -> storage/VPPs (Sunrun/Tesla 580MW/140k+ batteries, Sept heat wave) complement generation -> political pushback reinforces rather than reverses the BTM shift.

briefs.source_chain: MS's real neutral-rate estimate has risen from under 100bp to ~150bp since 1Q25, implying the current 3.75-4.00% funds rate is neutral-to-modestly-restrictive rather than accommodative, despite Chair Warsh framing the Sept hike as removing 'a dose of accommodation'; two FCI measures corroborate (FRBUS ~100bp tighter than end-Feb, driven mainly by higher 10Y yields; PCA at 0.78 std devs above average), both reading modestly restrictive but not unusually so; because policy isn't accommodative, the Fed doesn't need to catch up, so MS keeps its call for two more 25bp hikes (Dec, March) to 4.25-4.50%; FOMC minutes show only 4-5 participants saw policy as not/only-mildly restrictive, supporting a measured pace; separately, a 7th month of an oil-driven price shock has SPR at its lowest since 1984, and the effective tariff rate is rising from a 6.7% June-Aug average toward ~10% by year-end.
briefs.brief_chain: Neutral rate risen to ~150bp from <100bp since 1Q25 -> current 3.75-4.00% rate is neutral-to-modestly-restrictive, not accommodative, despite Warsh's 'removal of accommodation' framing -> FRBUS (~100bp tighter, driven by 10Y yields) and PCA (0.78 SD) corroborate, both modestly restrictive not unusually so -> policy not accommodative so Fed needn't catch up, maintains two more 25bp hikes (Dec/March) to 4.25-4.50% -> FOMC minutes (4-5 participants saw policy as not/mildly restrictive) support measured pace -> separately, 7th month oil shock with SPR at lowest since 1984, and effective tariff rate rising from 6.7% (Jun-Aug avg) toward ~10% by year-end.
